**STEP 3 - Items:** One whole apple. No oil, dressing or sauce is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The apple's projected area is 3.14 × (4)² ≈ 50 cm², about 9% of the plate. The rest of the plate is empty.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** A whole apple is roughly spherical, so its outer envelope is about 4/3 × 3.14 × (4)³ ≈ 270 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Whole fruit is denser than the cut-fruit range in the guide. A whole apple has a density of roughly 0.85 g/ml, so 270 ml × 0.85 ≈ 230 g. A medium 8 cm apple typically weighs 150–180 g, so I'll take the lower end of that range, about 170 g, as the better estimate.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Raw apple is about 52 kcal per 100 g. 170 g × 0.52 ≈ 88 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** One medium apple (about 170 g, around 90 kcal) is plausible for what is visible. The plate is mostly empty, which is consistent with a single fruit.
